hero.subheadline: Design a healing garden for Turin's Certosa Park, winner gets €7,500
hero.valueProposition: The winning proposal receives €7,500 to develop the design toward construction and becomes the basis for a real Healing Garden in Parco della Certosa.

content.whyJoin:
HEALING GARDEN is an international design contest run by Non Architecture and the first of six contests in the European project Sleeping Beauty, which aims to reactivate underused cultural landscapes through nature-based solutions inspired by the New European Bauhaus. Participants design a buildable urban prototype for healing within the intervention area of Parco della Certosa in Collegno, Turin.

The winner receives €7,500 to further develop the project, and the winning proposal serves as the basis for the realization of the garden within a €60,000 construction budget. Because the winning design can move toward a real built result, the contest offers participants a rare chance to see a competition entry carried into construction.

The contest is free to enter and open to all people of every age and cultural background, working individually or in teams of up to four. Selected projects gain visibility through publication on the Non-a contests website, which is viewed by a global community of architects and designers.
content.whoShouldApply:
This contest is for architects, landscape architects, urban designers, landscape and garden designers, and anyone with design training who can prepare a buildable concept for a garden within a defined site and budget. It is open to all human beings of every age and cultural background, working individually or in teams of up to four people.

Because the brief emphasizes biodiversity, social interaction, sensory experience, and heritage constraints, it suits designers with an interest in landscape ecology, therapeutic and healing landscapes, nature-based solutions, or heritage-sensitive design rather than purely visual concepts.

It suits designers comfortable working to a defined site, budget, and buildability brief, who are interested in nature-based solutions, healing landscapes, and heritage-sensitive design in a European context.

faq.question: Who is eligible to enter?
faq.answer: The contest is open to all human beings from every age and cultural background, working in groups or individually. Teams can be formed by a maximum of 4 people, and personal information for all team members is uploaded during submission. The contest has no registration fee.

faq.question: What are the prizes?
faq.answer: The winner receives €7,500 to further develop the project, and the winning proposal serves as the basis for the realization of the Healing Garden within a €60,000 construction budget. There are 9 honorable mentions and up to 20 finalists, whose projects are published on the Non-a contests website. Additional special prizes may be introduced.

faq.question: What is the registration and submission process?
faq.answer: Registration runs from April 15, 2026 to July 15, 2026 and is per submission or project. Participants must register in advance to obtain a valid registration code, then submit a single ZIP folder named with the registration code and project title via the official Google Form between July 15 and August 15, 2026.

faq.question: What should the design achieve?
faq.answer: The proposal should create a landscape environment that supports biodiversity, social interaction, and sensory experience, while respecting heritage constraints and the €60,000 construction budget. The project should function as an urban prototype demonstrating how design can foster well-being and ecological regeneration.

faq.question: Where is the contest site located?
faq.answer: The site is the defined intervention area of Parco della Certosa, located in Collegno within the metropolitan area of Turin, Italy. The intervention area has a total surface of approximately 25,600 m², and proposals must be developed within the boundary indicated in the official site documentation.

submissionGuide.detail: Complete the registration on the Non Architecture website between April 15 and July 15, 2026 to obtain a valid registration code. Registration is per submission or project and allows one project to be submitted.

submissionGuide.step: Download the brief and contest files
submissionGuide.detail: Download the contest brief in English or Italian and the official contest files, including the site documentation that defines the intervention area boundary and the €60,000 construction budget.

Design a buildable Healing Garden within the intervention area that supports biodiversity, social interaction, and sensory experience while respecting heritage constraints. Teams may include up to 4 people.

submissionGuide.step: Submit your project as a ZIP folder
submissionGuide.detail: Between July 15 and August 15, 2026, submit your project as a single ZIP folder via the official Google Form. Name the ZIP file using your registration code and project title.
The winner is announced between September 28 and October 2, 2026. The winning proposal receives €7,500 to further develop the design toward construction.
